findings.summary: APT is a free-software user interface that automates retrieval, configuration, and installation of software packages on Debian and Debian-like systems. It resolves dependencies, retrieves packages from configured repositories, and invokes dpkg in a topological sequence. APT includes command-line tools (apt, apt-get, apt-cache) and supports configuration via sources.list, preferences, and pinning to manage package versions and sources.

mechanisms.title: Dependency resolution and automated installation
mechanisms.explanation: APT retrieves and installs packages while automatically resolving and installing dependency packages, thereby preventing installation failures caused by missing dependencies.

mechanisms.title: Repository retrieval and package management
mechanisms.explanation: APT uses configuration files such as /etc/apt/sources.list to locate and retrieve packages from network or removable media repositories, and manages package index updates and version selection.
